title: Impact of Striped-Squirrel Nectar-Robbing Behaviour on Gender Fitness in Alpinia roxburghii Sweet (Zingiberaceae)
decision_basis: Primary predictor is robbed versus unrobbed state and outcomes are floral damage, pollinator visitation and reproductive fitness; no independent access-geometry predictor is tested against robbery route use.
notes: Robbery consequence study, not geometry-to-robbery test.

title: I’ve been robbed! – Can changes in floral traits discourage bee pollination?
decision_basis: Experiments manipulate robbery damage and nectar depletion to test subsequent pollinator response; robbery is the treatment rather than the route outcome predicted by pre-existing geometry.

title: Consequences of the high abundance of Bombus terrestris on the pollination of Vicia faba
decision_basis: Study quantifies legitimate visits and nectar robbery by visitor identity, year and flower age/resource depletion, but does not test an independently measured floral or visitor-flower access geometry predictor against route use.
notes: Route-resolved observations without focal geometry predictor.

title: Honey bees rob flowers after observing conspecifics and carpenter bees
decision_basis: Experimental predictor is observation of conspecific or heterospecific demonstrators and the response is switching to robbing; no floral access-geometry predictor is tested.

title: The Sensory and Cognitive Ecology of Nectar Robbing
decision_basis: Source is explicitly a review article synthesizing cognition and nectar robbing rather than an independent empirical biological study program.
notes: Secondary synthesis excluded from formal direct-study denominator.

title: Distasteful Nectar Deters Floral Robbery

notes: Important defence mechanism but outside frozen geometry predictor.

title: Breeding System and Response of the Pollinator to Floral Larceny and Florivory Define the Reproductive Success in Aerides odorata
decision_basis: Study asks how thieving/robbing/florivory alter pollinator behaviour and reproductive fitness; spur morphology is biological context but is not an independent geometry predictor modeled against robbery occurrence.
notes: Interaction consequence study rather than geometry-to-route test.
